articles.title: Maresca eyes rest for busy dad Haaland as Manchester City prepare for Porto
articles.summary: Norwegian forward has played every minute of season. Parenting duties have changed player’s ‘priorities’ Enzo Maresca believes Erling Haaland has become “complete” as his priorities have changed after the birth of the Manchester City No 9’s son two years ago.
body: Haaland has again started the campaign in prolific form, scoring three goals in City’s opening three Premier League victories. In three of the 26-year-old’s four previous seasons at City he has won the Premier League golden boot. Maresca pointed to how the birth of his son in 2024 changed the Norwegian’s motivation.

The manager said: “He’s a man now. He’s a dad. When he arrived here [summer 2022] he was not a dad and now he’s a dad and life completely changes because the priority becomes his son. I’m happy for him because he was already top as a player and as a boy but now you can see that he is complete now. He is a family man, he is still scoring goals so I’m very happy for him.”

City are at Porto in the opening Champions League league phase game on Tuesday. Haaland has played every competitive minute of the campaign so far, and Maresca said he will be rested at some point, particularly as the striker was part of the Norway team that reached the World Cup quarter-finals.

articles.title: Belichick denies he has lost control of UNC football program amid off-field turmoil
articles.summary: Former general manager has resigned post. Belichick’s son Steve is on medical leave. School has launched investigation into program. North Carolina football coach Bill Belichick said on Monday he believes his program “totally” has an atmosphere of following rules amid an investigation into its…
body: “Obviously everybody’s responsible, including me, for doing things properly,” Belichick said. “And we intend to do that.”

The Tar Heels were off following their season-opening win against TCU in Ireland on 29 August. But during that open week, general manager Michael Lombardi resigned after being put on paid administrative leave in late July amid the university’s investigation into his conduct.

The same day, Raleigh TV station WRAL cited anonymous sources in reporting the type of questions asked of some interviewees. Some focused on Belichick’s son Steve, the Tar Heels’ defensive coordinator, who is currently on medical leave. There have also been allegations that Steve Belichick has been questioned by lawyers over issues related to drug use.

Additionally, Lombardi attorney Tom Mars told The Athletic that the school’s investigation now included questions into potential “inappropriate” relationships that didn’t involve his client. Two people with knowledge of the situation had previously told the AP that a human resources complaint from a former employee was tied to Lombardi originally being placed on leave as the investigation launched.

articles.title: Emery ready to ignite Aston Villa’s season at Club Brugge after familiar slow start
articles.summary: Manager remains calm despite his side taking one point and scoring no goals in opening three Premier League games. Unai Emery is not panicking. He may kick every ball on the touchline but, behind closed doors, Aston Villa’s players are used to him being the calmest person in the room, routinely…
body: Emery, McGinn and Villa have been here before. Just last season, in fact; at this point, they were pointless in the Premier Leagueand still another 157 minutes from registering their first goal. So in one sense Villa, who shook off a slow start to qualify for the Champions League for the second time in three seasons, are ahead of schedule. Villa’s goalless draw at Hull on Saturday was not the most absorbing display but there were enough green shoots to trust Emery when he says he is confident they can again exceed expectations.

It is hard to disbelieve a man with Emery’s record, having overseen the most successful era in the club’s recent history. “When we started the project here, the ambition we had, it was [not even] in our highest expectations to be in Europe four years in a row,” the Villa manager says. “It was very difficult when we started working together but it was the ambition of the owner. We set our standards high with the players to be there and we are. Now is the moment to remember how we got here and the way we did. Now it is a different moment and chapter.”

articles.title: Zheng Qinwen erases another 5-0 deficit to stun Swiatek and reach US Open quarter-finals
articles.summary: Zheng makes astonishing recovery to win 7-5, 6-3. French Open champion Andreeva beats Potapova. The most important takeaway from 12 days at the US Open is simple: do not, by any means, lead 5-0 against Zheng Qinwen. No scoreline is as hazardous.
body: Somehow, two days later, Zheng repeated the trick in her very next set against a greater opponent. Down 5-0 in the opening set of her fourth-round match against the six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek, Zheng again locked down her game and reeled off seven games in a row to take the set. Zheng refused to let it go as she pulled off one of the best wins of her career, reaching the quarter‑finals of the US Open with a 7-5, 6-3 victory.

This was a remarkable turn of events for a wide variety of reasons. A player winning seven games in a row from 0-5 down in consecutive sets against two different opponents is almost unheard of at the highest level; doing so against two grand slam champions has never happened before.
“In one moment, I even forgot the score in the first set at 4-5,” Zheng said. “That shows how I am focused. I guess, to come back 0-5 [again] is not lucky, that’s [what] I can say.”

Swiatek was one of the tournament favourites after winning her first title of the year at the Canadian Open and she seemed to be on the way to rediscovering the confidence that has marked her as the greatest player of her generation.

articles.title: NFL Week 1 odds: Eagles favored to beat Commanders
articles.summary: Can you believe it? The first game of the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season is just days away! And there’s reason to believe the Birds are going to begin this year’s campaign with a win. The Eagles are 5.5-point home favorites against the Washington Commanders.
body: For the uninitiated, the home side is commonly favored by three points in a game between two evenly-matched teams. So, the Eagles are unsurprisingly viewed as the superior team in this matchup … on paper, at least.

If there’s anything unexpected about this line, it’s that the Eagles aren’t favored by more. Sure, it’s a division game and Week 1 brings uncertainty. But Philly’s roster is largely healthy while the Commanders are pretty banged up; Washington is most notably missing starting left tackle Laremy Tunsil. The Eagles’ front seven must take advantage and dominate up front.
The Commanders’ defense is going to be without starting cornerback Trey Amos, leaving Washington with a less than ideal outlook in the secondary.

Maybe Jayden Daniels carries his team largely like he did in 2024. Maybe Washington’s two new coordinators will make a big difference for them. Maybe the Eagles’ offense, which very much seems like a work in progress, has a slow start.

articles.title: What T.J. Bass’ stats tell us about replacing Tyler Smith
articles.summary: Before the 2026 season even starts, the Dallas Cowboys are facing their first challenge. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced on Monday that All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith is set to undergo surgery on his thumb and will be out for 4-6 weeks.
body: In his place, the Cowboys will go with veteran backup T.J. Bass, who has started in ten games over his career and played the most in a season last year, starting in five games.

Bass is not on the level of Smith, just facts. Very few in the NFL are close to Smith’s level of dominance. However, Bass is the perfect type of player for a situation like this based on his experience in live game situations, and with his knowledge of the offense, having been with Dallas since 2023.

Among all NFL guards last season to play at least 20 percent of the snaps, Bass had a 67.6 grade from Pro Football Focus. That ranked 31st out of 82 guards. His pass blocking and run blocking grades were also middle of the pack.
“I think he’s [Bass] played a lot of really good football for us, and we expect he’ll continue to do so.” Schottenheimer said during his press conference.

articles.title: Rybakina too strong for Osaka as Zheng stuns Swiatek at US Open
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to maintain her push for the world No 1 spot.
body: Rybakina will top the women's rankings if she reaches the semi-finals, and there is every chance she could leave Flushing Meadows as the new US Open champion after dismantling two-time winner Osaka on Louis Armstrong.
It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory.

"I played really well today. I was feeling the ball was really good from my side," the former Wimbledon champion said. "I was a bit lucky in some moments, found some lines, but super happy with the performance.
"Naomi is a tough opponent. I knew no matter the score I needed to focus on each ball as everything can change quickly. She is also a great player. I am glad how I played today.

articles.title: Manchester United agree deal to sign 16-year-old Liverpool prodigy
articles.summary: Manchester United are reported to have finalized an agreement to bring in Liverpool teenager Isaac Konde. The 16-year-old has reportedly completed all necessary procedures before his transfer to Old Trafford.
body: Acquiring promising youngsters from rival clubs has become increasingly prevalent in recent seasons, such as United's recent signing of Tynan Thompson from Tottenham Hotspur. Now, it appears that the Red Devils have wrapped up a deal for Konde, who has featured six times for Liverpool's Under-18s Premier League squad this season, registering one assist.

Konde typically plays on the left side of the attack, though he's just as capable of operating on the right wing. He came through Liverpool's youth system, but will now join their northwestern rivals, as per The Mirror.

Liverpool's most notable academy graduate of the past ten years has been Trent Alexander-Arnold, though he departed last summer for Real Madrid. Currently, they have players like Rio Ngumoha - who trained with England ahead of this summer's FIFA World Cup - and Conor Bradley coming through their system.

articles.title: Usyk's camp dismiss Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Joshua fight
articles.summary: Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua.
body: With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent.
Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024.
Responding to Fury's comments in a statement given to Sky Sports News on Monday evening, Usyk's manager Sergey Lapin said: "Usyk is not Tyson's backup plan.
"If Fury needs an opponent, he should visit the Ready to Fight platform. They can help him find a worthy opponent there.

articles.title: Pakistan investigating 'discipline and conduct' in latest twist on crisis tour
articles.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct" amid the team's crisis tour of England.
body: Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's to fall 2-0 down in the three-match series.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston, which begins on Wednesday.
A statement read: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.
"The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.
